questions.q: What does this lesson focus on, given that Lesson 24 already covered how snapshots capture history?
options: Using a snapshot's captured history correctly in analysis and reporting queries
How to configure the timestamp and check strategies from scratch
Re-explaining what dbt_valid_from and dbt_valid_to mean from zero
Deleting old snapshot rows to save storage
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly builds on Lesson 24 rather than repeating it — the new material is about querying a snapshot's history correctly.

questions.q: What goes wrong when a fact table is joined straight to a snapshot on the key column alone, with no effective-dating condition?
options: Every fact row fans out to match every historical version of that key, multiplying rows
The join simply fails and returns zero rows
Nothing goes wrong — snapshots only ever have one row per key
The warehouse automatically deduplicates the result
questions.explain: A snapshot has one row per historical version, so joining without an effective-dating filter multiplies every fact row by however many versions exist for that key.

questions.q: What condition does the 'as-of join' add to fix that multiplication problem?
options: A condition matching the snapshot version whose dbt_valid_from/dbt_valid_to window actually contains the fact row's date
A condition that only ever matches the most recent snapshot row
Removing the join entirely and using a subquery instead
Sorting the results by date with no filtering
questions.explain: The as-of join adds `date >= dbt_valid_from and (date < dbt_valid_to or dbt_valid_to is null)` so each fact row matches exactly the one version that was true at that time.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what does `region_at_time_of_order` represent?
options: The customer's region as it actually was when the order happened, not the customer's current region
The customer's current region only, ignoring history entirely
A random region assigned for testing purposes
The region where the dbt job physically ran
questions.explain: Using the as-of join, an order from before a customer moved regions still reports against the region that was true at the time of that order.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend building a `dim_customers_current` model filtered to `dbt_valid_to is null`?
options: Most downstream models only need today's value, so filtering to current once avoids repeating that filter in every model
It is required before any snapshot can be queried at all
It deletes historical rows from the underlying snapshot table
It is only useful for as-of joins, never for simple current-value lookups
questions.explain: For the common case of just wanting current attributes, a single current-only view lets every other model join like an ordinary dimension table.
